---
title: "Clone the repository"
---

Today you work in your own copy of the course repository,
so you can save your work as you go.

## 1. Fork the repository

1. Sign in to GitHub and open
   <https://github.com/chendaniely/MEDI-504A-2026W1-biostats>.
2. Click **Fork**, check that **Owner** is your own account,
   then click **Create fork**.

Your fork lives at
`https://github.com/<your-username>/MEDI-504A-2026W1-biostats`.

::: {.callout-warning}
Your fork is public.
Never put real patient data in it.
:::

## 2. Open your fork

Choose one.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Codespace

On your fork's page,
click **Code** → **Codespaces** → **Create codespace on main**.
It's the same setup as the [Codespaces](../setup-codespaces.qmd) page,
now saving to your fork.

### Positron

1. Copy your fork's URL from **Code** → **HTTPS**.
2. In Positron, run **Git: Clone** from the Command Palette
   and paste the URL.
3. Open the cloned folder.

### RStudio

1. Copy your fork's URL from **Code** → **HTTPS**.
2. **File** → **New Project** → **Version Control** → **Git**,
   and paste the URL.

:::

If you work on your own computer,
complete the [local setup](../setup-local.qmd) first.

## 3. Check it works

Open `example.qmd` and render it.
If it renders, everything you need for today is installed.

## Where things are

- `data/`: the data files for today
- `lecture-02/`: one file per section of today's lab;
  open each `.qmd` and work through it.
  The files that start with `07` to `09` are extra practice for after class.
- `homework.qmd`: the homework
  (the [Homework](../homework-instructions.qmd) page explains it)

Every file reads data with paths that start at the repository's top folder,
such as `read_csv("data/tumorgrowth_wide.csv")`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## RStudio: run chunks from the top folder

RStudio runs a chunk from the document's own folder by default,
so `data/...` paths fail.
Change **Tools** → **Global Options** → **R Markdown** →
**Evaluate chunks in directory** to **Project**.
Positron and Codespaces run code from the top folder already.
:::

## Save your work

Commit and push to your fork as you go:
in the **Source Control** panel (Positron, Codespaces)
or the **Git** pane (RStudio),
stage your changes, write a message, commit, then push.
